newsitem.title: CHINA: China spends $640 mln on Three Gorges resettlement.
newsitem.headline: China spends $640 mln on Three Gorges resettlement.

text.p: China spent 5.31 billion yuan ($639.76 million) from 1993 to the end of June this year on relocating people and industry displaced by construction of the huge Three Gorges dam, the Financial News said on Monday.

Spending was less than the 8.58 billion yuan allocated for the period from 1993 to the end of 1997, and also came in under the 6.915 billion yuan set aside in actual funds to be spent by the end of June this year, it said but gave no details.

Of the amount spent, 2.33 billion yuan went for the construction of new cities, 1.68 billion yuan was used to fund the transfer or construction of factories and mines and 660 million yuan was used to relocate farmers, the newspaper said.
Special infrastructure projects cost 640 million yuan, it said.

The Three Gorges hydoelectric dam across the Yangtze River, the world's largest water-control project, is designed to create a reservoir covering 1,084 square km (418 square miles) and will wholly or partly submerge two prefectural-level cities, 11 county seats, 114 towns and 1,599 factories, official media have said.
More than one million people are expected to be displaced with resettlement to continue until 2009 and predicted to cost 40 billion yuan at current prices.
